messages.content:
Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "can you help me write a friendly note for the people who use our shared bicycle shed before the weekly aisle check? The front aisle has to stay clear so everyone can get bikes in and out. We keep finding bikes parked across the painted line near the entrance, and I want the note to explain what will happen without sounding like anyone is being accused. If a bike is across that line and its owner’s name and unit number are readable on the frame tag, ask that owner to move it into a rack by the end of the day. If the tag is missing or the name or unit number can’t be read, don’t move the bike and don’t guess who owns it; put a reminder card on its handlebar asking the owner to move it into a rack by the end of the day. Please make clear that the second option applies only when the owner details aren’t readable, not when they are readable. Mention the weekly check, but don’t say that bikes will be removed, because that isn’t part of this arrangement. Keep the wording plain and friendly, and make it a note residents can read quickly. I’m asking for the notice text, not a change to the shed rules.", "output": "Draft a plain, friendly, quick-to-read notice for people who use the shared bicycle shed. Explain that the front aisle needs to stay clear so everyone can get bikes in and out, and mention the weekly aisle check. Use a non-accusatory tone.

Explain what to do when a bike is parked across the painted line near the entrance:
- If the owner’s name and unit number are readable on the frame tag, ask the owner to move the bike into a rack by the end of the day.
- If the tag is missing or the name or unit number can’t be read, don’t move the bike or guess who owns it. Put a reminder card on the handlebar asking the owner to move it into a rack by the end of the day. Make clear that this option applies only when the owner details aren’t readable.

Don’t say that bikes will be removed; that isn’t part of this arrangement. Write the notice text, without changing the shed rules."}]
